messages:
ashley: Endpoint vpce-0a1b2c3d4e in prod-us-west is stuck in PENDING for ~18m. Private DNS was enabled at creation. ENIs show 'creating'. Anyone seen this recently?

ryan: Which subnet(s) did you pick? interface endpoints create ENIs in each AZ subnet. can you paste `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0a1b2c3d4e` output?

ashley: pasted output: ```{
  "VpcEndpoints": [
    {
      "VpcEndpointId": "vpce-0a1b2c3d4e",
      "VpcId": "vpc-0abcde12345",
      "State": "pending",
      "SubnetIds": ["subnet-0f1e2d3c"],
      "PrivateDnsEnabled": true
    }
  ]
}```

infra-bot: AWS Event: ENI creation throttled / insufficient IPs for subnet subnet-0f1e2d3c (AvailableIpAddressCount=0)

liz: yup this is classic IP exhaustion. interface endpoint ENIs need an available IPv4 in each target subnet; if AvailableIpAddressCount=0 they stay pending. also check for overlapping private hosted zones that can mask the VPCE DNS name, but first fix IPs.

ryan: command to verify: `aws ec2 describe-subnets --subnet-ids subnet-0f1e2d3c --query "Subnets[0].AvailableIpAddressCount"` — what does it show?

ashley: ran it: `0`

liz: solution options: 1) recreate endpoint in subnets with free IPs, 2) free up IPs in that subnet (terminate/rehoming), 3) move service to different AZs. Quick test: try creating in subnet-0a2b3c4d (has room).

ashley: created endpoint with subnet subnet-0a2b3c4d and it went to 'available' within ~45s. `dig +short s3.vpce-012345.prod-us-west.vpce.amazonaws.com` returns `10.0.5.15`. ENI IDs attached: eni-0c1b2a3d.

ryan: good — SGs didn't block creation (they apply after ENI attach). follow-ups: add infra alert on AvailableIpAddressCount<10 for endpoint subnets and update runbook to check IP exhaustion before reporting PrivateLink failures.

liz: i'll open a ticket to add the alert and add a note about Private DNS collisions (Route53 private hosted zone with same name will take precedence).

ashley: thanks all, closing the thread. :thumbsup:
